transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-22
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Desai (CTO, Hawthorn), Luis Moreno (Infra Lead), Claire Ng (Compliance), Ethan Park (ML Eng), Maya Schultz (Procurement)

Auto-generated Summary (may be noisy):
Hawthorn is evaluating an on-prem, air-gapped deployment for inference workloads. Main ask: how do you deliver model and runtime updates without network egress, how signing and verification works, maintenance windows, and what hardware we support. They have older A40 nodes and strict USB policy.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros from our side, i'm samira, i'm the AE on this - and ravi is our solutions engineer. you can see the agenda in the calendar invite, but really want to hear about your constraints first.
[00:12] Priya: Hi Samira, thanks. i'm priya, CTO at hawthorn. we've got quite strict rules — no egress from our inference cluster, everything sits in a walled lab. luis will talk infra.
[00:20] Luis: hi all. we run a small GPU pool, mostly A40 cards, a couple of T4s for lighter work. network is air-gapped, only approved jump boxes in a DMZ. OS and firmware updates go through a signed media process.
[00:31] Ravi: got it. couple clarifying q's up front — when you say signed media, is that an internal CA that signs binaries, or do you use vendor-signed images?
[00:39] Claire: internal CA. we have a chain of trust process. anything we apply to the cluster must be signed, checksums validated, and logged for audit.
[00:46] Ethan: and to add, our maintenance windows are monthly and require a rollback plan. we can't have unattended automatic downloads.
[00:54] Samira: perfect, that's super helpful. the two broad options we typically discuss are: Redwood Private (on-prem with our control plane inside your network) vs Dedicated reserved capacity hosted in our datacenters. for air-gapped you obviously need Private. but there are still patterns for updates we can support.
[01:10] Priya: explain those update patterns, especially for model weights and runtime patches. we need to keep an audit trail and minimal manual steps.
[01:17] Ravi: sure. we often ship updates as signed bundles: model artifacts, runtime container images, and a manifest. in an air-gapped flow the bundle is exported to an encrypted USB or removable media, brought to the cluster via an approved operator, verified using your CA chain, and then applied. i'll sketch the runbook later.
[01:30] Maya: our procurement people will want clarity on the media handoff chain — custody, how many operators touch it, and how to verify authenticity.
[01:37] Samira: totally. we can include a custody checklist. one question for you: do you have a hardware HSM or KMS offline?
[01:44] Claire: we have an on-prem HSM but it's behind an internal network. keys for signing are kept in an HSM; however, the inference cluster doesn't have line-of-sight to the HSM.
[01:54] Ravi: that maps to a common pattern: sign artifacts inside the secure signing env (HSM), export signed bundle. on install, the agent verifies signatures with the embedded root cert. no need for the cluster to call back out.
[02:05] Luis: how do you handle model rollbacks? if an update fails, what's the guaranteed fallback?
[02:09] Ravi: we support atomic rollbacks — we stage the new model in a separate directory and swap symlinks if checks pass. if the runtime patch touches kernel level drivers that's trickier — we recommend testing in a staging air-gapped mirror of the cluster first.
[02:22] Priya: latency is also a concern — our inference p99 needs to be under 300ms for critical flows. does Redwood's runtime impose extra overhead compared to our current containerized tf-serving?
[02:31] Ravi: our runtime is optimized for GPU and has batching; for short sequences overhead is minimal — typically single-digit ms added. but real world numbers depend on model size and batching. we can run a benchmark in your environment as part of the pilot.
[02:45] Ethan: on that, can you run with quantized models? we don't have H100s here; A40s are limited.
[02:51] Ravi: yes, we support INT8/4 quantization variants and optimized kernels for A100/A40/T4 families. quantization reduces memory and improves throughput at the expense of small accuracy delta — we can include quantization recommendations.
[03:05] Maya: procurement ask — how long would a pilot cost commitment be?
[03:09] Samira: typically a 2-4 week pilot with dedicated support. for private deployments we do a scoped reserved capacity quote. i'll follow up with ballpark numbers.
[03:17] Priya: security really matters here. we need to surface audit logs for any update and verify tamper evidence on media. can you log the operator who applied the bundle and the exact commit/hash?
[03:27] Ravi: yes, each install action creates an immutable audit record: operator id, bundle manifest, checksums, and whether verification succeeded. those logs can be exported to your SIEM over the DMZ jumpbox if you can permit it; otherwise we can store them locally and include as part of the monthly audit package.
[03:44] Luis: what about model KV cache/prefix caching? can you warm caches without network?
[03:49] Ravi: cache warmers can run locally — we can ship a cache warming job in the bundle. note that some heuristics rely on request traces; but for initial warmups you can provide representative prompts.
[04:02] Priya: how do we handle compliance sign-off? Claire will need documentation for SOC2 and possibly ISO 27001 mapping.
[04:09] Claire: yes, the auditors will want to see separation of duties, key rotation, and signed update logs.
[04:14] Samira: we have a compliance package with SOC2 artifacts and an ISO mapping doc. i'll attach that after the call. it also includes RBAC and SAML SSO notes.
[04:23] Maya: any concerns about binary size? some of our older nodes have limited disk.
[04:27] Ravi: bundles can be delta-compressed and we support streaming installation to reduce disk spikes. model sharding is also an option if a single model is huge.
[04:37] Ethan: are you able to support offline telemetry for quality monitoring? we need to track hallucination rates and regressions locally and then ship metrics for audits periodically.
[04:46] Ravi: yes, we have a local quality monitor process that writes metrics to a local store. for audits you can export snapshots of the metric store or provide hashes. we avoid sending PII out of the cluster.
[04:56] Priya: how long would a full on-prem Private install take from kick-off to production? our timeline target is end of Q3.
[05:03] Samira: typically 6-10 weeks for a full Private deployment including security review, pilot, and rollout. depends on procurement and cert approvals. if you move faster on the CA and HSM details we can parallelize the runbook prep and scheduling.
[05:15] Luis: cluster resource constraints — we only have 3x A40s, 1x T4. will that meaningfully limit throughput for our expected qps?
[05:23] Ravi: it will cap peak throughput; we can size the concurrency and batch settings to fit the hardware. for example, lower concurrency with micro-batching to preserve latency. we can also suggest offloading some lower-priority requests to a small CPU fallback.
[05:37] Priya: what about emergency patches? suppose there's a CVE in the runtime, how quickly can you provide a signed patch and what's the operator flow?
[05:46] Samira: emergency patches follow the same signed bundle cadence but we can accelerate delivery and provide an emergency runbook. we'll also include a cryptographic hash and signature so you can verify integrity. production deployment would require an operator to apply during the nearest maintenance window; rollback steps are included.
[06:00] Claire: auditors will ask about key rotation. does Redwood recommend any rotation cadence for the root signing key?
[06:06] Ravi: typical rotation for signing keys is annually or after personnel change. because you have an HSM you can manage rotation inside your CA. we'll include a recommended process and integration notes for HSM-backed signing.
[06:18] Ethan: can we run a proof-of-concept that only exercises the model update path (no live traffic)? we want to validate signature verification and the audit logs first.
[06:27] Samira: absolutely — a dry-run POC is a standard step. we can do a model-only update test and verify logs and rollback without taking live traffic.
[06:34] Maya: procurement wants to ensure licensing terms — can we limit the scope to the cluster and have a time-limited pilot?
[06:39] Samira: yes. pilots are scoped. we'll put boundaries in the SOW.
[06:43] Luis: one more technical, do you support secure boot / attestation of the runtime?
[06:49] Ravi: we support an attestation hook where the runtime can upload a signed measurement, but in air-gapped setups that can be verified locally against a root of trust. we can show the exact flow in the technical deep-dive.
[06:59] Priya: ok good. can you explain how you handle model privacy — e.g., if we host proprietary models, how do you prevent accidental telemetry leakage?
[07:08] Ravi: by default our private agent collects minimal telemetry and it's configurable. for air-gapped installs we disable external telemetry and provide local-only logs. any metric exports must be explicitly enabled and go through your DMZ jumpbox.
[07:20] Samira: i'm going to share three docs after this call: (1) air-gapped security checklist, (2) pilot SOW template, (3) SOC2/ISO summary.
[07:28] Priya: great. and we'll share our CA root cert and an outline of our maintenance windows.
[07:32] Ethan: is there any recommended hardware upgrade to ease things? we could add an extra A40 or look at an H100 in the next procurement round.
[07:41] Ravi: adding another A40 helps throughput linearly, H100 would substantially increase perf but needs more power/cooling. we'll include perf projections for both.
[07:52] Maya: procurement question — do you have standard terms for on-prem support SLAs?
[07:57] Samira: yes, enterprise SLAs are available as an add-on; we can include a 99.9% uptime SLA on production nodes and guaranteed response times for critical incidents.
[08:06] Priya: for the pilot acceptance criteria: 1) successful signed bundle install test, 2) audit log verification, 3) p99 inference latency within our threshold on representative prompts, and 4) documented rollback. does that sound reasonable?
[08:19] Ravi: that's perfect and actionable. we'll bake those into the pilot test plan.
[08:24] Luis: quick note on storage: our nodes run 1TB NVMe per host. if you do local model caching, can we control eviction?
[08:32] Ravi: yes, cache size and eviction policy are configurable per node. we'll show recommended defaults for constrained disks.
[08:40] Claire: audit question — can we prove chain-of-custody for media? for example, a signed manifest plus operator biometrics?
[08:48] Ravi: biometrics is out of band for us, but we can include operator identity (SAML user) and multi-person sign-off recorded in the bundle metadata. you could combine that with your physical custody logs.
[08:59] Priya: okay, want to talk briefly about timelines. we need security sign-off by late June to hit end-of-Q3 target. is that feasible?
[09:08] Samira: yes, if we start pilot in May we can aim for production late Q3. procurement lead times and CA exchange are the usual friction points.
[09:17] Maya: final procurement note: we may need three vendor references. can you provide references of other regulated labs you've deployed Private to?
[09:25] Samira: yes, i'll include redacted references and case summaries.
[09:29] Priya: thanks. any open risk you see from your side?
[09:33] Ravi: main risks: hardware sizing (we'll need to validate perf), and time to exchange CA/HSM details. otherwise it's mostly procedural.
[09:41] Luis: for the POC, what's the support model? remote sessions? onsite?
[09:45] Samira: remote by default, but we can do a short on-site visit if required for the pilot kickoff — usually that's optional.
[09:53] Ethan: can you also include a checklist for operator training? our operators haven't run signed bundle installs before.
[09:59] Ravi: yes, a short operator runbook and a 2-hour training session is standard during pilot.
[10:06] Samira: recap: we'll send security artifacts, a pilot SOW, runbook draft, and references. hawthorn will share CA root cert, maintenance windows, and procurement timelines. next meeting: technical deep dive in two weeks.
[10:18] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[10:21] Claire: thank you.
[10:22] Maya: thanks.
[10:24] Samira: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache), speaker labels are correct but short interruptions present; timestamps are approximate.
questions: How will signed bundles be delivered and audited?
Can you support quantized models on A40s?
